section_summary: This section documents diplomatic and interdepartmental communications between April 1933 and February 1934 concerning radio interference caused by Japanese stations (principally JAQ and JFI) to U.S. Navy and Army communications in the Pacific. Although an informal bilateral conference of radio experts in Tokyo was initially proposed and planned by the State, War, and Navy Departments, Japanese authorities declined the meeting and suggested routing complaints directly to the Embassy. Concurrently, the Navy noted decreased interference while the Army experienced persistent disruption, leading both military departments ultimately to recommend abandoning conference plans and returning exclusively to standard diplomatic channels.

subfiles.about: Informs the Navy that Ambassador Grew is being instructed to bring station JAQ interference to the Japanese Government's attention.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Navy's letter of April 6 and reports Ambassador Grew is instructed to request Japanese elimination of JAQ interference on 8090 kc.
subfiles.title: Note from State Department to Secretary of the Navy regarding interference by station JAQ

subfiles.about: Instructs Ambassador Grew to make further representations to Japan concerning station JAQ's interference on 8090 kc.
subfiles.summary: Directs Grew to bring renewed Navy complaints regarding station JAQ interference on 8090 kilocycles to the Japanese Government's attention.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 251 to Ambassador Grew regarding interference from station JAQ

subfiles.about: Transmits diplomatic correspondence with Japanese Foreign Minister Uchida regarding interference by stations JAQ and JFI and notes proposal for expert discussions.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports on representations to the Japanese Foreign Office and encloses Notes 84 and 85 to Count Uchida alongside Uchida's reply (Note 25/T2). Uchida states JAQ and JFI will shift frequencies but denies using other complained frequencies. Grew reports the Japanese Vice Minister informally suggested expert bilateral discussions.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 345 from Ambassador Grew on Japanese wireless interference, with enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 345 regarding Japanese radio interference and solicits Navy's views on holding expert discussions.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Grew's despatch and enclosures regarding Japanese responses on JAQ, inviting Navy comments on the Japanese suggestion for expert discussions.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Despatch No. 345

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 345 regarding interference by stations JAQ and JFI and solicits War Department comments.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Grew's despatch regarding JAQ and JFI frequency shifts and requests War Department comments on proposed expert discussions.
subfiles.title: Letter from State Department to Secretary of War transmitting Despatch No. 345

subfiles.about: States that radio interference questions should be handled through diplomatic channels rather than expert discussions.
subfiles.from: Chief of Staff, War Department (Douglas MacArthur)
subfiles.summary: War Department welcomes Japanese frequency changes but advises keeping identical frequency issues strictly within diplomatic channels without technical expert conferences.
subfiles.title: Letter from War Department Chief of Staff Douglas MacArthur regarding interference discussions

subfiles.about: Reports serious radio interference to naval stations from stations JCT (Choshi), VVR (Mingaladon), and FRS (Saigon).
subfiles.summary: Navy reports severe interference from stations in Japan, British East India, and French Indo-China, requesting telegraphic protest instructions.
subfiles.title: Letter from Navy Department reporting additional radio interference in the Far East

subfiles.about: Clarifies that the interfering Japanese station at Choshi is listed as JCS rather than JCT.
subfiles.summary: Notes Bern Bureau lists station JCS, not JCT, at Choshi on 8200 kc, as confirmed by Lieutenant Freseman.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Treaty Division on station call sign JCS at Choshi

subfiles.about: Acknowledges Navy's report of May 19 regarding Far Eastern radio interference and states instructions are being sent.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Navy report on Far Eastern station interference and confirms appropriate instructions are being dispatched to eliminate it.
subfiles.title: Note from State Department to Secretary of the Navy acknowledging interference report

subfiles.about: Routing note requesting that the accompanying telegram be transmitted by naval radio.
subfiles.summary: Brief note indicating the telegram is to be sent by naval radio.
subfiles.title: Routing slip from Treaty Division to Communications and Records

subfiles.about: Instructs transmission of radio interference complaints to missions regarding stations JCS, VVR, and FRS.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Consul at Shanghai to forward representations against station JCS to Tokyo, station VVR to India, and station FRS to Saigon.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Consul at Shanghai for Tokyo, Mingaladon, and Saigon posts

subfiles.about: Records Lieutenant Freseman's report of May 21 interference by station JAQ on naval frequency 8090 kc.
subfiles.summary: Documents telephone report from Lieutenant Freseman that JAQ operated on 8089 kc on May 21, disrupting Navy transmissions on 8090 kc.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Treaty Division on station JAQ interference with Navy radio

subfiles.about: Instructs transmission of report on station JAQ operating off-frequency to the Embassy at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Directs transmission of 16th Naval District report regarding JAQ operating on 8089 kc on May 21 to Tokyo authorities.
subfiles.title: Telegram to American Consul at Shanghai regarding JAQ interference

subfiles.about: Endorses holding a limited bilateral conference of radio experts in Shanghai in late August.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Swanson welcomes the Japanese proposal for expert discussions, recommending a meeting in Shanghai in late August restricted to Pacific interference issues.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Navy Claude A. Swanson proposing expert conference in Shanghai

subfiles.about: Inquires whether Far Eastern Affairs will handle the proposed American-Japanese radio conference.
subfiles.summary: Transmits War Department letter concurring with Navy's conference proposal and asks FE if it will take charge of the case.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Treaty Division to Division of Far Eastern Affairs on proposed radio conference

subfiles.about: Concurs with the Navy Department's recommendation for an American-Japanese conference of radio experts.
subfiles.summary: Secretary of War concurs with Navy's recommendation to hold a conference of technical experts regarding radio interference in the Pacific.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern concurring in proposed radio conference

subfiles.about: Lists Navy and War Department representatives attending the morning interdepartmental meeting.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Laurence E. Salisbury)
subfiles.summary: Lists attendees for the July 7 interdepartmental meeting: Captain Hooper, Lt. Cmdr. Stone, Lt. Freseman, Major Colton, and Lt. Pachynski.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on attendees for interdepartmental meeting on radio interference

subfiles.about: Transmits War Department concurrence and proposes an interdepartmental conference on July 7.
subfiles.summary: Transmits War Department concurrence on expert talks, notes State has no funds for expenses, and invites Navy to a July 7 conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State Wilbur J. Carr to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Proposes an interdepartmental conference on July 7 to plan the radio interference talks.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges War Department concurrence on expert talks, clarifies expense policies, and invites representatives to an interdepartmental conference on July 7.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State Wilbur J. Carr to Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Discusses Navy's acceptance of conference proposal and potential retaliatory 'burning' of radio frequencies.
subfiles.summary: Discusses Navy concurrence in conference, suggests FE coordinate arrangements, and notes Navy practice of 'burning' interfering Japanese stations off frequencies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Treaty Division on interdepartmental handling of radio conference

subfiles.about: Suggests holding an informal meeting with Army and Navy representatives to expedite conference planning.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck suggests calling an informal meeting of Army, Navy, and State drafters to streamline arrangements for Tokyo instructions without protracted correspondence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Stanley K. Hornbeck suggesting informal interdepartmental meeting

subfiles.about: Refers radio conference matter to Protocol and Conferences Division as an international conference matter.
subfiles.summary: FE reviews background of interference disputes and recommends PC manage conference preparations, delegating logistics and expense commitments to War and Navy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Division of Far Eastern Affairs referring conference planning to Protocol and Conferences

subfiles.about: Returns conference file to Far Eastern Affairs due to the absence of division supervisors.
subfiles.summary: Dwight returns the radio interference papers to FE because Mr. Southgate is ill and Mr. Patterson is away.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from H. Gerald Dwight to Stanley K. Hornbeck returning conference papers

subfiles.about: Confirms agreement with July 3 suggestions and notes attendance of War Department delegates at July 7 conference.
subfiles.summary: War Department accepts suggestions and notes arrangements made with Salisbury for two representatives at the July 7 interdepartmental meeting.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern accepting meeting arrangements

subfiles.about: Records discussions among State, War, and Navy representatives concerning holding the radio conference in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Stanley K. Hornbeck and Laurence E. Salisbury)
subfiles.summary: Representatives discussed holding the technical conference in Shanghai versus Tokyo. While Hooper and Colton initially favored Shanghai for financial reasons, Hornbeck successfully advocated Tokyo to expedite decisions and utilize attachés. Navy and Army agreed to investigate funding for Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Proposed Conference with Regard to Japanese Radio Interference

subfiles.about: Requests that the State Department arrange the expert conference in Tokyo on or after October 1, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Navy agrees to holding the conference in Tokyo on October 1 or thereafter, designating the Naval Attaché and Asiatic Fleet Radio Officer.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Navy W. H. Standley requesting conference in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese Note No. 48/T2 reporting frequency shifts for stations JAQ and JFI.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses Count Uchida's note of June 16, reporting station JAQ successfully shifted to 8050 kc and station JFI will shift to 8605 kc.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 435 from Ambassador Grew transmitting Foreign Office note on frequency shifts

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 435 reporting the frequency shift of Japanese station JAQ.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copy of Grew's Despatch No. 435 indicating station JAQ shifted to 8050 kc on May 5.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State William Phillips to Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 435 reporting frequency shifts for stations JAQ and JFI.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Despatch No. 435 reporting frequency shifts of JAQ to 8050 kc and upcoming shift of JFI to 8605 kc.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State William Phillips to Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Agrees to hold the radio interference conference in Tokyo on or after October 1, 1933.
subfiles.summary: War Department agrees to holding the informal conference in Tokyo on October 1 or thereafter and requests representative nomination from Manila.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern agreeing to Tokyo conference

subfiles.about: Records Major Colton's request for instructions sent to Tokyo and notes copies sent to War and Navy.
subfiles.summary: Notes request by Major Colton for instructions sent to Tokyo; copies of Telegram 70 forwarded to Colton and Hooper.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on sending telegram copies to Major Colton and Captain Hooper
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Confirms Commander Stone's statement that Navy and War agree on conference limitations.
subfiles.summary: Records telephone conversation with Lt. Cmdr. Stone confirming Navy and War agreement on agenda limitations set in Navy's June 3 letter.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Laurence E. Salisbury on Navy and War agreement on conference scope
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Instructs the Embassy to informally propose a technical radio conference in Tokyo on or after October 1.
subfiles.summary: Instructs Grew to informally propose an informal conference of radio experts in Tokyo on or after October 1, strictly limited to Pacific interference.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 70 to American Embassy Tokyo directing conference arrangements

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Note 124 and Foreign Office reply Note 55/T2 regarding off-frequency operations of JCS and JAQ.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses Note 124 protesting off-frequency transmissions by JCS and JAQ, and Foreign Minister Uchida's reply stating JAQ maintained its frequency and JCS operators were instructed on proper adjustment.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 463 from Ambassador Grew transmitting correspondence on JCS and JAQ interference

subfiles.about: Transmits copy of Tokyo Despatch No. 463 regarding interference from stations JCS and JAQ.
subfiles.summary: Forwards copy of Grew's Despatch No. 463 with enclosures concerning interference from stations JCS and JAQ.
subfiles.title: Note from State Department to Secretary of the Navy transmitting Despatch No. 463

subfiles.about: Designates Captain Fred P. Andrews as War Department representative for the Tokyo conference.
subfiles.summary: Requests that Captain Fred P. Andrews, Signal Corps, represent the War Department at the Tokyo radio conference.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern designating Captain Fred P. Andrews

subfiles.about: Records Commander Stone's statement that Navy prefers to defer the Tokyo radio conference.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Laurence E. Salisbury)
subfiles.summary: Stone informed FE that Navy is in no hurry for the Tokyo conference; War Department concurs in deferring decision.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Navy recommendation to defer the radio conference
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Speculates that Japanese stations may have deliberately interfered with U.S. naval communications to test effectiveness.
subfiles.summary: Speculates that Japanese radio interference might have been intentional testing against U.S. Asiatic Fleet communications during strained relations, ceasing once confirmed effective.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by EHD speculating on intentional Japanese radio interference
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Recommends deferring decision on the Tokyo radio conference until December 1, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Navy reports reduced interference and recommends waiting until December 1 before deciding on a conference; War Department concurs.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Navy Henry L. Roosevelt recommending conference deferral

subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese authorities deem a conference unnecessary and suggest direct reporting to the Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities decline expert conference, proposing military authorities cable future complaints directly to the Embassy for Department of Communications investigation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 147 from Ambassador Grew reporting Japanese rejection of conference

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy on procedure for transmitting interference complaints pending interdepartmental review.
subfiles.summary: Directs Embassy to route complaints through Foreign Office and consult Department before acting on any direct complaints from Manila.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 88 to American Embassy Tokyo regarding complaint channels

subfiles.about: Notes receipt of War Department letter and request for similar letter from Navy before drafting instructions.
subfiles.summary: Notes attached War Department letter and requests matching Navy letter before drafting instructions to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by EHD on War Department letter and instruction drafting

subfiles.about: Reports approval by Major Colton and Commander Stone of draft telegram to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Reports Major Colton approved draft telegram and indicated War Department will request continuing official diplomatic complaint channels.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by EHD on draft telegram consultation with Colton and Stone

subfiles.about: Reports Commander Stone's call stating Navy awaits Army initiative on Tokyo suggestion.
subfiles.summary: Stone phoned stating Navy is waiting for Army initiative on the Japanese suggestion regarding interference.
subfiles.title: Note by Laurence E. Salisbury on Navy awaiting Army initiative

subfiles.about: Internal reference slip noting numbers 17 and 121.
subfiles.summary: Division slip noting reference numbers 17 and 121.
subfiles.title: File routing slip with reference numbers 17 and 121

subfiles.about: Notes that the conference was informally suggested by the Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Brief note recording that the conference proposal originated informally from the Japanese Vice Minister.
subfiles.title: Note on origin of expert conference suggestion
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Brief note regarding who first approached the Japanese on the conference.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note inquiring who first approached the Japanese regarding conference talks.
subfiles.title: Routing note on initial conference discussion
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs files

subfiles.about: Details Major Colton's strong objections to allowing local commanders to bypass official channels.
subfiles.summary: Reports Major Colton's objections to direct Manila-Tokyo reporting, stressing worsening Army interference, mainland station concerns, and need for standard diplomatic channels.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by EHD on Major Colton's objections to direct reporting to Embassy

subfiles.about: Recommends abandoning conference plans and confining interference matters strictly to diplomatic channels.
subfiles.summary: Dern rejects direct reporting from Orient commands as uncoordinated across wide military areas, recommending abandonment of conference plans and retention of strict diplomatic channels.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War George H. Dern recommending termination of conference plans

subfiles.about: Informs War Department that Tokyo Embassy has been instructed to drop conference plans and use diplomatic channels.
subfiles.summary: Confirms Embassy Tokyo is instructed to drop conference plans and submit complaints only by State Department direction.
subfiles.title: Note from State Department to Secretary of War confirming instructions to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits Federal Radio Commission report on International Radiotelegraph Convention violations by Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Federal Radio Commission tabulation of Japanese ship radio violations under 1927 Washington Convention for presentation to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 442 to Ambassador Grew regarding Japanese ship radio violations

subfiles.about: Concurs that an informal conference is unnecessary and recommends submitting reports through State.
subfiles.summary: Navy concurs that an informal conference is unnecessary and recommends continuing to submit interference reports through State.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of the Navy W. H. Standley concurring with War Department

subfiles.about: Informs Navy Department that Tokyo Embassy has been instructed to drop conference plans.
subfiles.summary: Informs Navy that Tokyo Embassy is instructed to drop conference plans and present complaints only via State.
subfiles.title: Note from State Department to Secretary of the Navy confirming instructions to Tokyo

subfiles.about: Directs Embassy Tokyo to cease arranging a conference and communicate interference complaints only under Department direction.
subfiles.summary: Transmits War and Navy letters concurring that expert conference plans be dropped, instructing Embassy to present interference complaints only under State Department direction.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 457 to Ambassador Grew instructing termination of conference efforts
